doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Monk, Ellington and Archie Shepp in the 1970s
title: Last gigs with Monk and a methadone counselor job
summary: Ware works as a counselor and plays with Monk opposite Blood, Sweat and Tears and at Syracuse.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: came through pretty good. And I worked -- for a while, while I was working -- I'm going to get back to something. I was working with Thelonius, we had another job. I got a job -- this was before I met Gloria -- working as a counselor in one of those methadone drug abuse programs and that's when I went back with Thelonius again. Only this time, we had Philly Joe Jeffrey Jones on drums, Paul Jeffries on tenor and myself. We was working opposite Blood, Sweat and Tears.

We had a job in Philharmonic Hall and that was kind of weird. All these electronic Blood, Sweat and Tears and the Thelonius Monk acoustic quartet. But we played and I had this job, like I said, as a counselor. I worked at it about three months. Monk said, "Well, we got to go up to Quebec." We had a job up there, university, Canada. On our way back, we were to play the Arena in Washington. Syracuse. We played the University of Syracuse with that same group -- Philly Billy Joe, Paul and myself.
Let's see. That was about the end of the Thelonius Monk gigs.
